source_title: Canelo Álvarez wins back world title as Houthi attacks cast shadow over Riyadh

Mexican star wins unanimous decision over Mbilli

Mexico’s Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez reclaimed the WBC super-middleweight title with a unanimous-decision victory over the previously unbeaten Christian Mbilli in Riyadh on Saturday night.
The fight went ahead at Kingdom Arena despite a week of heightened security concerns in the Saudi capital, where the Saudi-led coalition said it had intercepted missiles and drones launched by Iran-aligned Houthi forces. Several events in the kingdom were cancelled or postponed, including the Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition.
Álvarez, 36, fighting for the first time in more than a year, relied on his trademark counter-punching and precise body shots to overcome the aggressive French champion and re-establish himself among boxing’s elite.
The judges scored the contest 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110 in favor of the Mexican. (The Guardian had it 117-110 .)
“It’s something unbelievable. It feels like my first title. Now, after 21 years as a professional, 16 years ago I won my first title. Now I won that title again. I’m so proud of my team,” ‌Canelo said in English.
“I love boxing. That’s why I’m here, because I still love boxing and I enjoy it a lot.”
Mbilli, who entered the fight with a record of 29 wins and one draw, sought to unsettle Álvarez with relentless pressure and a higher volume of punches. But the challenger landed the cleaner blows, including a sharp uppercut that staggered Mbilli in the seventh round.
The victory marked a significant comeback for Álvarez, who suffered only the third defeat of his professional career when Terence Crawford outpointed him by unanimous decision in September 2025.
That loss cost Álvarez his undisputed super-middleweight crown , ending his reign as holder of the division’s four major titles.
The contest took place three weeks after a missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300. A second projectile struck a passenger terminal the following day, according to the Saudi-led military coalition, while several international airlines suspended flights to the kingdom amid the mounting threat to civilian aviation.
Turki al-Sheikh, the chairman of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority and one of boxing’s most influential power brokers, said earlier this month that Álvarez had personally assured him he would go ahead with the fight regardless of the security situation. “Canelo reached out and told me he’ll still fight in Riyadh this October, no matter what happens,” Al-Sheikh wrote on social media. “He fears nothing.”
The escalation threatened Saudi Arabia’s ambitions to establish itself as a global destination for major sporting events. The kingdom has become a dominant force in professional boxing under Al-Sheikh, using its considerable financial resources to attract some of the sport’s biggest names, even as its expanding sporting footprint has drawn scrutiny over its human rights record and accusations of sportswashing.
Álvarez made a brief, apparently oblique reference to the circumstances surrounding the fight during his post-fight remarks, thanking family members who were watching from afar rather than ringside.
“I also want to thank my family, who are watching me from afar today for the first time,” he said in Spanish. “My siblings, my parents, my daughters, my son, and my wife – who also couldn’t make it due to certain circumstances.”
Álvarez did not elaborate on those circumstances or explicitly link their absence to the security situation.
Mbilli, 31, had been elevated to full WBC champion following Crawford’s departure from the division , having previously held the interim title.
The Cameroon-born boxer fought to a split draw against Lester Martínez on the undercard of the Álvarez-Crawford showdown, ending a run of 29 consecutive professional victories.
Saturday’s result improved Álvarez’s record to 64 wins, three defeats and two draws and handed Mbilli the first loss of his professional career.

## मैक्सिकन स्टार की शानदार वापसी

मेक्सिको के अनुभवी बॉक्सर साउल "कैनेलो" अल्वारेज़ ने रियाद के किंगडम एरिना में हुए मुकाबले में क्रिश्चियन म्बिल्ली को सर्वसम्मति से हराकर डब्ल्यूबीसी सुपर-मिडिलवेट विश्व खिताब फिर से हासिल कर लिया है। 36 वर्षीय अल्वारेज़ ने अपनी शानदार काउंटर-पंचिंग और सटीक बॉडी शॉट्स के दम पर फ्रांसीसी चैलेंजर म्बिल्ली को मात दी। जजों ने यह मुकाबला 115-112, 116-111 और 117-110 से अल्वारेज़ के पक्ष में स्कोर किया।

यह मुकाबला ऐसे समय में हुआ जब सऊदी राजधानी में सुरक्षा संबंधी चिंताएं थीं और रियाद में क्षेत्रीय तनाव की खबरें सामने आई थीं। हालांकि, सऊदी-नेतृत्व वाले गठबंधन और अधिकारियों की व्यवस्था के बीच यह मुकाबला आयोजित किया गया।

## मुकाबले की मुख्य बातें

* **अल्वारेज़ का अनुभव:** 21 साल के पेशेवर करियर वाले अल्वारेज़ ने सितंबर 2025 में टेरेंस क्रॉफोर्ड के खिलाफ मिली हार के बाद इस जीत से जोरदार वापसी की है।
* **म्बिल्ली की पहली हार:** इस मुकाबले से पहले 29 जीत और एक ड्रा का रिकॉर्ड रखने वाले म्बिल्ली के पेशेवर करियर की यह पहली हार है।
* **सुरक्षा और आयोजन:** रियाद में हालिया तनाव और सुरक्षा चिंताओं के बावजूद यह मुकाबला तय कार्यक्रम के अनुसार आयोजित हुआ, हालांकि कुछ अन्य सांस्कृतिक और खेल आयोजन रद्द या स्थगित किए गए थे।

## व्यावहारिक निहितार्थ और सत्यापन

खेल प्रेमियों और विश्लेषकों के लिए यह मुकाबला बॉक्सिंग जगत में एक बड़ा मोड़ है, क्योंकि अल्वारेज़ ने अपनी श्रेणी में फिर से शीर्ष स्थान हासिल किया है। आधिकारिक परिणामों और खेल संगठनों की घोषणाओं की पुष्टि के लिए डब्ल्यूबीसी (WBC) की आधिकारिक वेबसाइट या संबंधित खेल संघों की घोषणाओं को देखा जा सकता है।

en_body:
## Álvarez Triumphs via Unanimous Decision

Mexican boxing star Saúl "Canelo" Álvarez reclaimed the WBC super-middleweight title with a unanimous-decision victory over Christian Mbilli in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, according to a report by The Guardian.

The bout took place at Kingdom Arena on Saturday night. Judges scored the contest 115-112, 116-111, and 117-110 in favor of the 36-year-old Álvarez, handing the previously unbeaten French challenger the first professional defeat of his career.

## Context and Security Concerns

The event proceeded despite heightened regional tensions and security concerns in the Saudi capital. Reports indicated that several other events in the kingdom had been recently cancelled or postponed following intercepted missile and drone activity from Houthi forces, alongside prior regional incidents involving King Khalid International Airport.

Key details surrounding the event include:
* **Fighter Records:** The outcome improved Álvarez's professional record to 64 wins, three defeats, and two draws.
* **Previous Bout:** The fight marked Álvarez's return following a unanimous-decision loss to Terence Crawford in September 2025.
* **Promotional Ambitions:** The match highlighted Saudi Arabia's continued push to host major international sporting events under the General Entertainment Authority.

## Post-Fight Comments

Speaking after the victory, Álvarez expressed pride in his performance and longevity, noting his return to the top tier of the division after 21 years as a professional. During his post-fight remarks, he also thanked family members who watched the event from afar due to unspecified circumstances.

Readers seeking to verify the original reporting can consult the published round-by-round coverage and official sanctioning body records from the event.
